speaker: Doctor

Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned an episode of loss of consciousness; can you tell me exactly what you were doing right before you passed out?

Did anyone witness the event and observe any jerking movements or blue coloring of your skin?

Also, have you experienced any chest pain, shortness of breath, or a racing heart recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasovagal Syncope secondary to micturition (commotio cordis/micturition syncope).

Given the classic presentation of syncope occurring immediately after urination in a 53-year-old male, this is highly suggestive of micturition syncope or commotio cordis. I will now request an ECG to rule out underlying structural heart disease or arrhythmia. REQUEST TEST: ECG
